[h5]TL;DR: Recommended only for the story and lore. Play at the easiest difficulty and auto all battles with the tbfix mod. Or just watch it on YouTube. The battle system only feels good when playing against bosses.[/h5]

The main story is ok. The side stories connected to it are very interesting. But I don’t like the ending, and some of the side characters’ conclusions are meh. I kinda like the short VN skits. I like the world lore concept.

If you really want to play fast, I suggest installing the tbfix mod. You will get an overall speed-up when you change FPS from 60 to 30. Make sure to turn it back to 60 FPS before quitting. It only works if your game starts at 60 FPS settings. I experienced 3 crashes so far after boss fights, probably because of tbfix. [b]The default move speed and battle speed feel too slow for me.[/b]

Each equipment piece has mastery EXP skills that you gain through battles. The more mastery you gain, the easier the game becomes. Good thing it is not linked to equipment enhancement. Equipment enhancement is really annoying, especially the random abilities gacha. There are exclusive abilities for each equipment piece that are also unlocked at random enhancement levels. Dismantling results are also based on each equipment’s random abilities.[b]W T F[/b]. Materials being capped at 99 is a problem. [b]The buying, selling, and dismantling process/menu is very bad in this game.[/b]

After several equipment masteries, battles become easy and you can turn on auto-battle. For mob fights, I auto-battled for 3/4 of the game at the highest difficulties possible (Hard -> Intense -> Chaos) while speeding up the game. There are a few tough bosses that make you suffer on Chaos difficulty. [b]All the auto-battling made me feel like the battle system is unpolished; they should’ve just added a skip button lol.[/b]

Mini-games exist just for costumes/cosmetics. There is variety, but not all are fun. Some cosmetics are indeed charming.

The EX Dungeon post-game allows you to farm mats and new equipment, plus extra costumes and events. [b]You're a masochist if you play this dungeon on Chaos difficulty.[/b]

[b]I don’t like that there is a Dire Foe Boar you can defeat at the start that changes your whole mats/equipment gain for the entire playthrough.[/b] I had no idea it existed until near halfway through the game, when I triggered the first Dire Foe. So cringe.

[b]There are a lot of flashbangs after battles, warps, traps, and cutscenes.[/b]

My first tales game I got into, knew nothing about the tales series and got this game out of curiosity. Easily one of my top 5 games in terms of storytelling and top 3 RPG games I ever played. This game breathed and felt like a traditional fantasy JRPG, it doesn't feel like a typical hero adventure story as it revolves around the protagonist Velvet who is far from being a hero and is more of a personal revenge quest that involves some rich character development from her and supporting characters which I felt was so well done. She as a character I really liked and was a key driving point of how good the story was with the stakes and world building. Combat wise I was impressed, there's a lot to learn and understand how the combat system works but not too complex, but what made it challenging was the difficulty as it was my first playthrough I went on "Hard" mode which wasn't the highest difficulty as there were two more higher difficulty levels, but on this mode I definitely felt the struggle and died numerous times in battle from Boss fights to common enemies while in turn made it much more rewarding each battle I win. The lore and power systems are really cool and fascinating and was really nice how its incorporated in combat and the story. 

Overall a 10/10 game experience for me and cannot recommend it enough for anyone wanting to get into the Tales series or is looking a great JRPG experience.

[h2] Это одна из лучших JRPG, которые я играл [/h2]

Я никогда не видел, чтобы история (это не особо спойлер) велась от лица «злодеев». Это буквально чернющая история. История про персонажей со своими судьбами, верой и принципами, которые остаются неизменными до конца, неважно, что происходит вокруг. Это просто восхитительная история. Ещё в Zestiria они показали мне, что сделали идеальных персонажей, но тут они просто снесли мне голову нахер. Это восхитительно, когда каждый персонаж ощущается как отдельный главный герой; как человек, который готов в любой момент сделать то, что должен, то, что хочет, просто потому, что он идёт с тобой из-за СВОИХ интересов. Он в любой момент может тебя бросить и уйти. Ты ощущаешь его не как должное, а как напарника по интересам. И это тебе всегда показывают.

Единственная похожая игра — FF7. Там была серая мораль: главные герои боролись с корпорацией, но из-за этого вредили простому населению. Здесь то же самое, но во много-много раз более масштабно, черно и эгоистично. Я просто потрясён экспириенсом. Это стандарт качества, который они, к сожалению, не смогли преодолеть в Arise. Я согласен со всеми, кто считает Berseria лучшей частью.

Они сделали мир по-фалконовски, хоть и не настолько масштабно и качественно: добавили много NPC со своими историями; тонны сайдквестов, которые дополняют мир и историю различных персонажей (порой спрятанных, которых нужно досконально искать в мире); гига длинный данж с платформами, который ♥♥♥♥♥♥ вымораживал в каждом Trails. В играх Falcom к NPC всегда было много внимания: они создавали свои истории для каждого персонажа. Буквально любой NPC имел свою историю, которую ты мог наблюдать, если общался с ним по мере прохождения сюжета. Это одна из сильнейших сторон Falcom — и они добавили это в Tales: NPC реагируют на события в мире, дают тебе инфу о монстрах, инфу о том, что происходит в других местах. Одно удовольствие читать диалоги NPC. Falcom — единственные, кто создавал NPC как главных героев. Из части в часть они усовершенствовали это мастерство, и уже к 4–5 играм им не было равных. Из Trails они взяли лор для NPC, добавили самих персонажей (а они делают лучших персонажей и их проработку, как я уже убедился за все игры, что прошел) — и вышла бомба, которая мне очень зашла.

Я без иронии считаю эту игру одним из самых качественных и уникальных экспириенсов в мире JRPG.

Геймплей стал классным. Он меняется в зависимости от сложности. Он даже лучше, чем в Arise. Беготни хоть и меньше, чем в Zestiria, но тоже немало. Сюжет сразу затягивает, он очень драйвовый. Исследование мира довольно интересное.

Я люблю сюжеты Tales за то, что они непредсказуемы. Ты боишься за персонажей, за конец, потому что разрабы вообще никого не щадят. У тебя нет ощущения сюжетной брони. И ты поймёшь это, когда пройдёшь Zestiria и Berseria. 

Сила Trails — в сюжете и иммерсивности мира (NPC, раскрытие, масштаб, глубина, музыка). Сила Tales — в персонажах: их раскрытии, харизме и взаимодействии.
Те же Final Fantasy, Persona, Ys и другие менее известные серии JRPG не могут похвастаться ничем из этого. Музыкой, наверное, только. Я не говорю, что они посредственны. Мне нравятся эти игры, но того, что показывают создатели Tales и Trails, они показать не могут. Престол этих аспектов никто ещё не превзошёл.

I bought this game on a whim, and as my first entry into the Tales series, it was quite an experience. The story is a breath of fresh air because it's darker than your typical RPG. You start as Velvet Crowe, a doting sister to her brother Laphicet, until a tragic event during a 'Scarlet Night' changes everything. Velvet ends up with a demonic left hand as a Therion and sets out for revenge. The mid-game plot twist provides amazing character build-up. Regarding gameplay, the Linear Motion Battle System allows you to map various Artes to your buttons to create your own combos. I struggled a bit with optimizing them and often ended up just button-mashing (definitely a skill issue, haha!). Exploration is the main downside; character movement feels sluggish on such massive maps, which sometimes made me sleepy. Still, a solid game. 7.8/10.

Wow, che gioco meraviglioso, non l'avete ancora giocato, vi invidio, vorrei essere al vostro posto, per ricominciarlo senza conoscerlo e potermelo godere come fosse la prima volta. Qualcun'altro l'ha scritto in altre recensioni, questo è un gioco che tratta argomenti molto, molto profondi, in maniera tutt'altro che banale. Durante il vostro viaggio in Berseria, avrete modo di ridere e piangere, davvero! I personaggi e le loro storie, vengono approfonditi a tal punto che vivrete certe scene con totale trasporto emotivo, e sono sicuro che tutti loro resteranno nel vostro cuore una volta terminato il gioco. Io, per puro caso, ho iniziato Berseria subito dopo aver terminato Zestiria, senza sapere che fosse collegato e ambientato centinaia di anni prima. Questo mi ha permesso di avere la storia di Zestiria fresca fresca nella mia mente, e poter fare tutti i collegamenti tra i due giochi, man mano che andavo avanti con Berseria. Quando lo finerete, capirete perché ho iniziato questa recensione con "wow", è un viaggio profondo, bellissimo, emozionante. Detto questo, gameplay frenetico e appagante, i combattimenti non vi stancheranno, sono molto divertenti (niente a che vedere con Zestiria, l'unico "Tales of" che non mi è piaciuto a livello dei combattimenti). Non temete, i soldi spesi per l'acquisto di questo gioco, saranno un ottimo investimento, non lo dimenticherete di sicuro!

I had this game sitting in my Steam library for about 9 years - not because I didn't care to play it, but because I didn't have a computer that could run it. Flash forward to today, having finished must be over a hundred games in the past 3 years with a much stronger PC, and I can now say the LONG due completion was VERY much worth it.

This is a very long game, boasting a story that will, at times, make you laugh and smile...but more often than not, the tale contained within is more dark than not. It's a story of vengeance, one that will have you rooting for the protagonist, even when the other characters within will be doing the opposite. Personally, there are times at work when I was still thinking about some of the most emotionally charged moments in the game...it's a powerful narrative with a lot of attention to detail.

The gameplay is a blend of traditional Tales Of elements (real-time combat across an expansive battlefield), with notable differences in the combat - the main ones being lack of TP for using artes, and artes themselves being the sole forms of attack, split into 3 categories: Martial, Hidden, and Malak (equivalent to spells from older games). Instead of TP, the Soul Gauge serves as a form of "limiter" to prevent you from just spamming attacks constantly, which can be frustrating compared to the older games, where all you needed to do was just make sure you had a steady supply of TP for artes as needed. Artes can be configured at any time in the menu, allowing you to set any learned arte to a specific button in a sequence of up to 4 (which reminds me of a very similar system in God Hand, a game I hold very near and dear to my heart). It can take some getting used to for both series vets and newcomers alike, but overall I think my nitpicks are outweighed by how well the devs managed the execution of the system overall, in my opinion.

I strongly recommend picking this one up and giving it a shot if you haven't already; there's a remaster coming out towards the end of the month, as you may already know, but Bandai Namco has a slight history of flubbing classic titles when remastering them, so give the remaster a bit to marinate and garner reviews first before diving right in. From what I can tell so far though, it looks like MUCH more bang for your buck, since it comes at a cheaper price(!!) with some of the DLC (especially character costumes) from the original release added in. Whatever way you can get your hands on this game though, whether it's this original release or the remaster coming soon, you don't wanna miss it - this is a tale to remember, and a lot of people HAVE remembered, quite fondly.
